name: Wrestling
title: Become a Wrestling Official in Southwest Florida | GNOA
description: Learn rules, scoring, positioning, signals, and match management to officiate wrestling in Naples, Collier County, and Southwest Florida.

sections.subhead: Stay in the sport. See every position differently.
paragraphs: Wrestling officiating puts you close to the action and challenges you to make clear, confident decisions in a sport where control, position, timing, and safety all matter.
You'll learn rules, scoring, positioning, signals, communication, judgment, and how to manage a match from start to finish.
Greater Naples Officials Association recruits, trains, and develops new and experienced wrestling officials throughout Naples, Collier County, and Southwest Florida.

image.alt: Wrestling official crouched close to two wrestlers on the mat, whistle in mouth, watching for control

sections.heading: Close Action. Quick Decisions. Strong Judgment.
sections.intro: Wrestling happens fast and often within inches of the official. A takedown, reversal, near fall, escape, or potentially dangerous situation can develop in seconds. Good officials learn how to move, maintain the right angle, recognize control, and make decisions with confidence.

items.title: Stay Close to Wrestling
items.text: Continue being part of the sport you enjoy from a completely different perspective.

items.title: Learn the Craft
items.text: Rules matter, but so do positioning, timing, scoring, communication, and judgment.

items.title: Protect the Competitors
paragraphs: Safety is a major part of wrestling officiating.
Officials need to recognize potentially dangerous situations and act quickly when necessary.

items.title: Challenge Yourself
items.text: Every match brings different styles, positions, and situations.

sections.heading: Never Officiated Before?
paragraphs: You don't need previous wrestling officiating experience to get started.
GNOA helps new officials learn the fundamentals and become more confident as they gain experience.
sections.after: You won't learn everything in your first match. You build it one match at a time.

items.text: Complete the short form and select Wrestling.

items.text: We'll explain training, registration, equipment, the season, and what you should expect.

items.title: Learn the Fundamentals
items.text: Study the rules, practice positioning and signals, and learn how to recognize scoring situations.

items.text: Start with assignments that match your training and experience.

items.title: Keep Getting Better
items.text: Work matches, receive feedback, learn from experienced officials, and continue developing.

sections.heading: What Makes a Good Wrestling Official?

items.title: Positioning
paragraphs: Officials need to move constantly to maintain the best possible view of the action.
The right angle helps you recognize control, scoring, and safety situations.

items.title: Rules Knowledge
paragraphs: Wrestling has detailed rules involving scoring, control, penalties, boundaries, and match situations.
Training helps you learn how to apply them in real time.

items.title: Judgment
paragraphs: Not every situation is obvious.
Good officials learn to recognize what happened, determine control, and make clear decisions without guessing.

items.title: Communication
items.text: Signals, voice, body language, and communication with coaches, wrestlers, and the scorer's table all matter.

items.title: Composure
paragraphs: Matches can become intense.
Good officials stay calm, professional, and focused on the action in front of them.

sections.heading: The Match Starts to Look Different
lines: Your first few matches may feel like everything is happening at once.
Position. Control. Scoring. Time. Safety. The boundary. The next move.
With training and experience, you begin to recognize patterns and anticipate where the action is going.
You stop trying to see everything at once.
You get better at seeing what matters.

But don't buy everything before talking with GNOA.
Depending on current requirements, equipment may include:

info.callout: Talk to us first. See what's available. Buy what you need.

items.q: Do I need previous officiating experience?
items.a: No. GNOA trains and develops new wrestling officials.

items.q: Do I need to have wrestled?
items.a: No. Wrestling experience can help with familiarity, but officiating is its own skill and can be learned.

items.q: Will I start with varsity matches?
items.a: New officials develop over time. Assignments should match your training, experience, and readiness.
Officials need to move constantly around the mat, change levels, and maintain good positioning throughout the match.

items.q: Is safety part of the official's job?
items.a: Yes. Officials are responsible for recognizing potentially dangerous situations and protecting the competitors while allowing legal action to continue.
Talk with GNOA first. We can help you understand current requirements and whether used or hand-me-down equipment may be available.

sections.title1: Ready to See Wrestling From This Side?
paragraphs: You already know what the sport looks like from the stands.
Officiating gives you a completely different perspective.
